payload.rebuttal: fixed: restore_mutant no longer locates the edit by searching the file for mutant.replace. apply_mutant now records the byte offset where the single find match was replaced, in a new MutationResult.offset field, alongside the existing displaced bytes. restore_mutant takes the whole MutationResult and slices the file at [offset, offset + len(replace)) directly — verifying that span still equals mutant.replace as a safety check before writing displaced back in its place. This works identically whether replace is empty or not, since it never needs to count or search for occurrences of replace in the file at all. Added test_a_deletion_mutant_with_an_empty_replace_also_restores, which applies a mutant with replace="" and asserts the round trip restores the file exactly.
